raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py`) applies the decode-context-parallel (DCP) owner/local transform to **every** KV cache group whenever `CP_SIZE > 1`. Before this PR the CP branch was unconditional:

```python
virtual_block_size = kv_block_size * CP_SIZE
virtual_block_indices = positions // virtual_block_size
virtual_block_offsets = positions % virtual_block_size
is_local = virtual_block_offsets // CP_INTERLEAVE % CP_SIZE == cp_rank
...
local_positions = virtual_block_indices * kv_block_size + local_offsets
```

Only full-attention and MLA KV is actually sharded across DCP ranks. Groups holding **replicated** per-rank state index *global* positions on every rank:

* Mamba/GDN recurrent state (`MambaSpec`),
* sliding window and chunked local (`SlidingWindowSpec`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`),
* the `KpoolTailSpec` scratch group (`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:970`, a `SlidingWindowSpec` subclass with block size 4).

For those groups the transform is wrong twice over: `is_local` PADs out `(cp_size - 1) / cp_size` of their tokens, and the tokens that survive are rewritten to `virtual_block_indices * kv_block_size + local_offsets`, i.e. the wrong slot. It fails silently — no assert, no shape error, just corrupted state.

The rest of the stack already knows which groups are sharded: `dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec(spec, dcp_world_size)` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:709`) returns the process DCP size for `FullAttentionSpec`/`MLAAttentionSpec` and `1` for everything else, and `KVCacheCoordinator` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:143`) and the offload manager (`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py:304`) already route through it. The slot-mapping kernel was the one place that did not.

**The fix**

* `BlockTables.__init__` takes a per-group `cp_enabled: list[bool] | None` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py:30`), stored and uploaded next to the existing `slot_mapping_enabled` (`:55`, `:123`) and passed to the kernel (`:229`).
* The kernel loads `group_cp` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py:349`) and gates the CP branch on it: a non-CP group owns every token (`is_local |= group_cp == 0`, `:353`) and keeps its global positions (`local_positions = tl.where(group_cp, ..., positions)`, `:359`).
* `GPUModelRunner.initialize_kv_cache` derives the list per group from `dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec(spec, self.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size) > 1` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:605`) and passes it to `BlockTables` (`:675`).

`cp_enabled` defaults to all-`True`, so `CP_SIZE == 1` and every existing caller behave exactly as before; the only behaviour change is for a non-full-attention group under DCP > 1.

**Scope.** This is not a theoretical case: any Mamba+attention hybrid running `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` has a replicated Mamba group alongside sharded attention. DeepSeek-V3.2 never tripped it because it has neither a Mamba group nor a kpool tail group. The change is hardware-agnostic — Python config plumbing plus a predicate in an existing Triton kernel, no new kernel and no device-specific code.

**Provenance.** Found while designing decode-context-parallel support for GLM-5.3-Flash's pooled DSA indexer on 4x NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80) with an out-of-tree Ampere sparse-attention backend. Neither that model's DCP support nor that backend is part of this PR — the pooled indexer still rejects DCP upstream, so this PR does **not** enable DCP for it. The fix is preventive there and a live correctness fix for the hybrid models that do run DCP today.

> Note: this PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change, the tests and all results below were reviewed and run by the submitter.

## Test Plan

New unit tests, in the style of the files they join:

* `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`
  * `test_slot_mappings_localize_only_context_parallel_groups[cp_rank=0..3]` — two groups under `cp_size=4`, one `cp_enabled=True` (block size 16) and one `cp_enabled=False` (block size 4). The sharded group must match the localized reference; the replicated group must get global positions with **no** `PAD_SLOT_ID`.
  * `test_slot_mappings_localize_every_group_by_default` — omitting `cp_enabled` yields `[True]` and the old localized mapping, pinning the no-op default.
* `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`
  * `test_initialize_kv_cache_enables_cp_only_for_dcp_sharded_groups` — a `FullAttentionSpec` + `MambaSpec` config at `decode_context_parallel_size=8` must reach `BlockTables` with `cp_enabled == [True, False]`. Captures the `BlockTables` kwargs the same way the neighbouring `test_qsa_circular_group_uses_custom_slot_mapping` does, so it needs no GPU.

Commands:

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
```

Plus `ruff format` / `ruff check` and the runnable `pre-commit` hooks on the changed files.

## Test Result

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
8 passed, 14 skipped
```

`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py` carries a module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda())`, so the five new cases there are gated the same way as the file's existing tests and are among the 14 skipped on the macOS box the final run was done on. **They have not been executed on CUDA in this state and need a CUDA runner to go green** — a reviewer confirming that would be welcome. The eight that ran include the new model-runner test, which exercises the derivation.

The expectations the CUDA tests assert were cross-checked offline against a line-by-line transcription of the patched kernel (40 checks over `cp_rank` 0-3, `cp_interleave` 1/2/8, `cp_size` 1 and 4, and `slot_mapping_enabled` both ways). That transcription also confirms the failure mode: with `cp_enabled` forced `True` on the block-size-4 replicated group at `cp_size=4`, exactly 48 of 64 tokens (three quarters) come back as `PAD_SLOT_ID` and the remaining 16 land on wrong slots — matching the reported symptom.

`ruff format` and `ruff check`: clean on all four files. `check-spdx-header`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-torch-cuda-call`, `check-boolean-context-manager` and `check-root-lazy-imports`: pass.

Hardware tested: the correctness argument is hardware-agnostic (Python config plumbing plus a Triton predicate). The investigation ran on 4x NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80, 64 GB); no GPU was available for the final test run, which is why the CUDA-gated cases are reported as skipped rather than passing.

Rebased on `main` at a615f533; applies cleanly.

files.patch:
@@ -212,6 +212,142 @@ def test_dcp_slot_mapping_with_smaller_kernel_blocks(cp_rank: int):
     assert torch.equal(actual, expected)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cp_rank", range(4))
+def test_slot_mappings_localize_only_context_parallel_groups(cp_rank: int):
+    """Only DCP-sharded groups get localized slot mappings.
+
+    Full-attention/MLA KV is sharded across DCP ranks, but groups holding
+    replicated per-rank state — Mamba/GDN recurrent state, the
+    ``KpoolTailSpec`` scratch — index global positions on every rank.
+    Localizing those would PAD out the tokens this rank does not "own" and
+    write the surviving ones to the wrong slots.
+    """
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    cp_size = 4
+    num_tokens = 64
+    sharded_block_size = 16
+    replicated_block_size = 4
+    sharded_block_id = 5
+    replicated_block_ids = list(range(20, 20 + num_tokens // replicated_block_size))
+
+    block_tables = BlockTables(
+        block_sizes=[sharded_block_size, replicated_block_size],
+        max_num_reqs=1,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=num_tokens,
+        max_num_blocks_per_group=[1, len(replicated_block_ids)],
+        device=device,
+        kernel_block_sizes=[sharded_block_size, replicated_block_size],
+        cp_size=cp_size,
+        cp_rank=cp_rank,
+        cp_interleave=1,
+        cp_enabled=[True, False],
+    )
+    block_tables.append_block_ids(
+        req_index=0,
+        new_block_ids=([sharded_block_id], replicated_block_ids),
+        overwrite=True,
+    )
+    block_tables.apply_staged_writes()
+
+    idx_mapping = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor([0, num_tokens], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    positions = torch.arange(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    slot_mappings = block_tables.compute_slot_mappings(
+        idx_mapping,
+        query_start_loc,
+        positions,
+        num_tokens_padded=num_tokens,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    # Sharded group: this rank owns every cp_size-th token (cp_interleave 1)
+    # and packs the tokens it owns densely into its local block.
+    assert slot_mappings[0].tolist() == _localized_slots(
+        num_tokens, sharded_block_size, [sharded_block_id], cp_size, cp_rank
+    )
+    # Replicated group: global positions, and no token is padded out.
+    assert slot_mappings[1].tolist() == _global_slots(
+        num_tokens, replicated_block_size, replicated_block_ids
+    )
+
+
+def test_slot_mappings_localize_every_group_by_default():
+    """``cp_enabled`` defaults to all groups, preserving the previous
+    behaviour for callers that do not pass it."""
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    cp_size = 4
+    cp_rank = 1
+    num_tokens = 64
+    block_size = 16
+    block_id = 5
+
+    block_tables = BlockTables(
+        block_sizes=[block_size],
+        max_num_reqs=1,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=num_tokens,
+        max_num_blocks_per_group=[1],
+        device=device,
+        kernel_block_sizes=[block_size],
+        cp_size=cp_size,
+        cp_rank=cp_rank,
+        cp_interleave=1,
+    )
+    assert block_tables.cp_enabled.tolist() == [True]
+
+    block_tables.append_block_ids(
+        req_index=0, new_block_ids=([block_id],), overwrite=True
+    )
+    block_tables.apply_staged_writes()
+
+    idx_mapping = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    query_start_loc = torch.tensor([0, num_tokens], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    positions = torch.arange(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    slot_mappings = block_tables.compute_slot_mappings(
+        idx_mapping,
+        query_start_loc,
+        positions,
+        num_tokens_padded=num_tokens,
+    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+    assert slot_mappings[0].tolist() == _localized_slots(
+        num_tokens, block_size, [block_id], cp_size, cp_rank
+    )
+
+
+def _localized_slots(
+    num_tokens: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    block_ids: list[int],
+    cp_size: int,
+    cp_rank: int,
+) -> list[int]:
+    """Reference for the DCP-localized slot mapping, cp_interleave == 1."""
+    virtual_block_size = block_size * cp_size
+    slots = []
+    for position in range(num_tokens):
+        virtual_offset = position % virtual_block_size
+        if virtual_offset % cp_size != cp_rank:
+            slots.append(-1)
+            continue
+        local_position = (
+            position // virtual_block_size
+        ) * block_size + virtual_offset // cp_size
+        slots.append(
+            block_ids[local_position // block_size] * block_size
+            + local_position % block_size
+        )
+    return slots
+
+
+def _global_slots(num_tokens: int, block_size: int, block_ids: list[int]) -> list[int]:
+    """Reference for a non-context-parallel group: global positions, no PAD."""
+    return [
+        block_ids[position // block_size] * block_size + position % block_size
+        for position in range(num_tokens)
+    ]
+

+    class FakeAttnCGSupport:

+    monkeypatch.setattr(

🚀

Closing in favour of #56723, which I missed when opening this: it adds the same per-group gate (`dcp_sharded` per `BlockTables` group, `is_local = ~sharded | is_local`, `local_positions = tl.where(sharded, ...)`) and predates this PR by four days.

Two things from this PR that may still be useful there:

1. The regression tests here (`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`: a sharded block-16 group next to a replicated block-4 group at `cp_size=4`, checked against a Python reference for each rank; `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py`: `FullAttentionSpec` + `MambaSpec` at DCP=8 must reach `BlockTables` as `[True, False]`). Happy to port them onto #56723 if wanted.
2. One thing worth confirming on #56723's default: with `AttentionSpec.dcp_sharded = True` and the override coming from `impl.dcp_world_size`, `SlidingWindowSpec` / `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` groups stay marked sharded unless their backend reports `dcp_world_size == 1`. Here the flag was derived from `dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec(spec, dcp) > 1`, which yields `False` for those spec types (and for the `KpoolTailSpec` single-block scratch that motivated this, a `SlidingWindowSpec` subclass).

Investigation assisted by Claude Code.
